claims.wording: TinkerTool exposes additional personal preference settings already built into macOS.
claims.excerpt: TinkerTool is an application that gives you access to additional preference settings Apple has built into macOS.
claims.conditions: Not hands-on evidence; whitespace normalized from saved text.

claims.wording: The vendor lists TinkerTool 11.71 (Build 260910), released September 14, 2026, as a 5.4 MB notarized macOS DMG.
claims.conditions: Separate table cells; vendor notarization and size statements, not binary inspection. No DMG downloaded.

claims.wording: The current generation lists macOS 26 Tahoe and macOS 27 Golden Gate. For macOS 13 Ventura, 14 Sonoma or 15 Sequoia, the vendor directs users to TinkerTool 10 (10.6).
claims.excerpt: TinkerTool 10; macOS 13 Ventura macOS 14 Sonoma macOS 15 Sequoia; 10.6
claims.conditions: Vendor OS labels only; do not turn into a blanket macOS 13+ claim for 11.71. CPU architecture and independent Apple release status are not verified.

claims.wording: TinkerTool is a no-charge download; software redistribution requires prior written permission.
claims.excerpt: You can download the application TinkerTool at no charge. ... Distributing the software without prior written permission is prohibited.
claims.conditions: No currency/billing period for a no-charge download. No open-source licence or full EULA established. This software restriction is not proof of screenshot permission or prohibition.

claims.wording: The vendor says changes affect the current user, need no administrative privileges, and can reset to Apple defaults or the pre-TinkerTool state.
claims.excerpt: preference changes can only affect the current user. You don't need administrative privileges ... All preference settings changed by TinkerTool can be reset to Apple's defaults, or to the state that existed before using the tool.
claims.conditions: Not a safety guarantee or file backup. Privacy permission exceptions are documented separately in TT08.

claims.wording: TinkerTool and TinkerTool System are separate complementary applications: personal preferences versus administrator-level settings affecting all users.
claims.excerpt: The tools do not share any duplicate settings or features, they complement one another.
claims.conditions: See section What is the difference between TinkerTool and TinkerTool System? Do not import System cleanup features or prices.

claims.wording: Documented Finder options include showing hidden/system files and suppressing creation of .DS_Store files on network volumes; available settings vary by OS version.
claims.excerpt: Enable the Finder to show hidden and system files; Disable the creation of hidden Finder .DS_Store files on network volumes
claims.conditions: Separate feature-table rows marked supported for listed 26/27 variants. Showing files does not authorize deleting them; preventing creation does not remove existing files.

claims.wording: Some protected-app preferences require Full Disk Access; deleting TinkerTool does not undo changed preferences. The FAQ describes resetting settings and logging out/in.
claims.excerpt: Settings affecting critical areas, such as Time Machine, Mail, and Safari are disabled in TinkerTool until you confirm to macOS that the application can have Full Disk Access. ... Applications will respect their settings no matter if TinkerTool is on your disk or not.
claims.conditions: FAQ headings Will TinkerTool access any of my private files? and I used TinkerTool for a while... No settings changed or removal performed. Do not recommend broad permissions for the Finder workflow.

claims.wording: Export/import can transfer eligible preference settings between accounts or computers; settings dependent on third-party applications are excluded from the stated transferable set.
claims.excerpt: export and import the settings, copying them to another user account or to a different computer. All settings which don't depend on the availability of third-party applications can be transferred.
claims.conditions: Documentation, not a migration test or full Mac backup.

claims.wording: Breathing Room, which we build, is a free macOS 13+ maintenance preview; the identified 0.1.0-preview.1 release is Apple Development signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized, and discloses Python 3.10+ prerequisites.
claims.excerpt: Published preview says Apple Development signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized. ... Python 3.10+ is a disclosed prerequisite for disk inventory and legacy scripts, not bundled.
claims.conditions: Excerpt from capabilities.md lines 48–51 summarizing retained release inspection, not a direct quote of the public release. Universal installer advertised; physical Intel and clean-machine runtime unverified.

claims.wording: Breathing Room source implements storage views, app/helper CPU-memory grouping, local activity history and constrained cleanup approvals; source presence does not establish installer parity or measured results.
claims.excerpt: Source implementation is not proof that every feature works in the distributed installer.
claims.conditions: capabilities.md lines 24–40 and cited source paths. Optional verified Ruff-cache automatic Trash mode and exact saved daily approvals prevent unconditional never-deletes-without-asking language.

claims.wording: Optional hosted AI requires authentication/internet and can receive paths/process/storage context; advertised AI Care is $5 USD/month or $50 USD/year, renewing until cancelled, with applicable tax at checkout.
claims.excerpt: Confirmed advertised $5 USD/month, $50 USD/year. ... Plans renew until cancelled; applicable tax shown at checkout.
claims.conditions: capabilities.md lines 58–86. Free local capabilities are separate; paid quotas/entitlement enforcement and checkout operation not tested. Website download account gate differs from public GitHub release access.

workflow.primaryIntent: Distinguish changing Finder visibility/network-folder preferences from reclaiming Mac storage.
workflow.title: Showing hidden files is not a Mac cleanup plan
workflow.description: TinkerTool changes personal Finder preferences; revealing hidden files does not make them disposable. Separate visibility changes from a storage investigation before choosing a tool.
outline: Official Finder visual after lead, only after rights clearance
Choose the TinkerTool generation for your exact macOS version (TT02, TT03)
Separate showing hidden files, preventing network .DS_Store creation and deleting existing data (TT07)
Record/reset preference changes: removing the app is not rollback (TT05, TT08)
If the question is disk growth, investigate storage owners rather than toggle Finder preferences (BR02, disclosed affiliation)
Decision checklist and limitations, plus comparison/hub links
workflow.interactionPass: Planned non-mutating decision checklist: appearance/visibility -> OS-matched preferences; current disk usage -> inventory; recurring growth -> qualified activity investigation. No commands, cleanup execution, simulated measurements or settings changes.
